references.text: John the Baptist quotes directly from [ref:Jes 40:3|Isaiah 40:3]: "A voice of one calling in the wilderness: Prepare the way for the Lord!" This is the prophecy he identifies with – he is the voice crying out in the desert, making a path for the Lord.
[ref:Matt 3:3|Matthew 3:3] applies the same prophecy from Isaiah 40:3 to John the Baptist, where the evangelist Matthew confirms that John is the voice calling out in the wilderness.
[ref:Mark 1:3|Mark 1:3] also quotes Isaiah 40:3 as fulfilled in the ministry of John the Baptist, and begins his entire gospel with this prophecy.

[ref:Luk 3:4-6|Luke 3:4-6] gives the longest quotation from Isaiah 40:3-5 in connection with John the Baptist's preaching in the wilderness, expanding the quote to include that "all flesh shall see God's salvation".

The broader context of [ref:Jes 40:1-5|Isaiah 40:1-5] is about comfort for Israel and preparation for the Lord's coming. John the Baptist understands his role in light of this prophecy – he is the forerunner who makes a path.
[ref:Mal 3:1|Malachi 3:1] prophesies about a messenger who will clear the way before the Lord. This is a related prophecy that was also fulfilled in John the Baptist as the Messiah's forerunner.

[ref:Joh 1:6-8|John 1:6-8] introduces John as a man sent by God to testify about the light. Verse 23 explains how John himself understood his role – not as the Messiah, Elijah, or the Prophet, but as the voice preparing the way for the Lord.

[ref:Joh 1:19-22|John 1:19-22] gives the immediate context where John denies being the Christ, Elijah, or the Prophet. The answer in verse 23 is his positive identification of himself through the Isaiah prophecy.
[ref:Jes 62:10|Isaiah 62:10] uses similar language about making and clearing a way for the people, pointing to the preparation that John the Baptist called Israel to before the coming of the Messiah.
[ref:Joh 3:28-30|John 3:28-30] confirms John the Baptist's self-understanding from 1:23 – he was sent ahead for Christ and must decrease while Christ increases.
